items.title: LASTMA warns against skate shoes on highways
items.description: The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has cautioned children, teenagers and young adults against using rolling skate shoes, wheeled footwear and similar devices on public highways. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, gave the warning in a statement on Sunday in Lagos. Bakare-Oki warned that such practices exposed users to grave and entirely avoidable traffic hazards. “The authority observed that the increasing use of footwear fitted with concealed or retractable wheels on roads designed primarily for motorised traffic constitutes a serious safety concern. “This is particularly where users attempt to glide alongside moving vehicles, cross carriageways indiscriminately or manoeuvre through traffic without adequate protective measures and adult supervision,” he said. He noted that unlike designated recreational facilities, public highways were dynamic and highly unpredictable environments characterised by the simultaneous movement of vehicles, motorcycles, pedestrians and other road users. “The introduction of wheeled recreational devices into such spaces can significantly diminish a user’s ability to respond appropriately to sudden vehicular movements,. “This creates circumstances capable of culminating in devastating collisions and life-altering injuries. “LASTMA therefore strongly advises parents, guardians, schools and caregivers to discourage children and other vulnerable road users from engaging in recreational activities involving roller skates on highways, expressways, bridges and service lanes. “They should also be discouraged from engaging in such activities in other locations where vehicular traffic is permitted,” he said. The LASTMA boss further urged users of such footwear to restrict their activities to designated recreational areas, private compounds or other safe environments specifically suited for skating. He added that they were to utilise appropriate protective equipment, including helmets, knee pads, elbow pads and other safety gears. Bakare-Oki reiterated that road safety is a collective responsibility that requires constant vigilance, discipline and respect for the inherent risks associated with public roads. He emphasised that the preservation of human life must remain paramount, noting that no recreational activity was sufficiently important to justify exposing oneself or other road users to unnecessary danger. “Motorists should exercise heightened vigilance around children and young persons using wheeled footwear, particularly within residential areas, estates, school zones and other locations where vulnerable road users may suddenly enter the traffic stream,” he said. He urged members of the public to promptly report dangerous traffic situations, road obstructions, crashes, breakdowns and other incidents requiring urgent traffic-management intervention through the LASTMA toll-free short code 3367. This, he said would facilitate timely intervention by relevant responders. The post LASTMA warns against skate shoes on highways appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Faux justificatifs et dépenses floues : Vaste traque aux anomalies comptables dans le secteur associatif
items.description: Les magistrats de la Cour des comptes ont accéléré le rythme de vastes missions de contrôle visant à auditer les finances et les activités d'associations ayant bénéficié, au cours de la période écoulée, de subventions financières accordées par des collectivités territoriales et des établissements publics, avec un accent particulier mis sur les factures, les justificatifs de dépenses et la conformité des dépenses déclarées avec les projets et activités effectivement réalisés. Hespress a appris de sources bien informées que les opérations d'audit en cours ont ciblé plus de 2 750 associations actives dans divers domaines, ayant obtenu des financements publics dans le cadre d'conventions de partenariat et de soutien. Les mêmes sources précisent que les magistrats des comptes ont entrepris le réexamen des documents comptables, des pièces justificatives de paiement et d'un échantillon de factures fournies pour justifier les dépenses, ainsi que la vérification de la nature des prestations et des équipements acquis grâce à ces fonds. Ces mêmes sources soulignent que les missions d'audit se sont concentrées sur des associations opérant notamment dans les domaines du sport, de l'animation culturelle, de la promotion touristique et des activités sociales et de développement. Il a été procédé à une vérification rigoureuse du respect des engagements figurant dans les conventions de financement signées, en comparant les programmes qu'elles s'étaient engagées à exécuter avec les réalisations effectives sur le terrain, ce qui a permis de déceler des indicateurs de dysfonctionnements dans la gestion des budgets de ces associations. Selon les mêmes sources, les anomalies relevées comprennent, outre des incohérences dans la facturation des dépenses, des lacunes et un désordre dans la documentation comptable d'opérations financières effectuées par voies bancaires et hors canaux bancaires. S'y ajoute la faiblesse des mécanismes de suivi de certains bailleurs de fonds quant au sort des crédits transférés aux associations bénéficiaires. Ces constats ont poussé les équipes d'audit à élargir leurs vérifications au circuit de dépense des fonds et aux documents utilisés pour justifier ces charges. Le montant global des subventions publiques faisant l'objet de ce contrôle s'élève à environ 664 millions de dirhams (66,4 milliards de centimes), ce qui a renforcé le niveau d'exigence quant à la validité des factures présentées en contrepartie des prestations et des achats, en particulier après la constatation d'écarts entre la valeur des dépenses déclarées et le volume ou la nature des réalisations supposées avoir été financées. Les magistrats des comptes ont décelé, parmi les dossiers soumis à l'examen, des soupçons liés à la valeur de factures présentées pour justifier diverses dépenses, ainsi que des documents émis par des fournisseurs dont certaines transactions suscitent des doutes quant à la régularité des factures. Les opérations de vérification s'étendent ainsi à la nature même des prestations réglées, aux prix figurant sur les documents et à l'existence de preuves matérielles attestant de l'exécution des opérations déclarées. Dans le même contexte, les sources précisent que les équipes d'audit ont été confrontées, dans d'autres cas, à l'incapacité de responsables d'associations à fournir des pièces justificatives pour des dépenses portant sur des montants importants. Cela a nécessité le recours aux autres documents comptables et relevés bancaires disponibles pour retracer le parcours des crédits, déterminer leur affectation et les comparer aux engagements préalablement fixés dans les conventions de financement. Les opérations d'audit ont également englobé les mécanismes de contrôle adoptés par les collectivités territoriales et les établissements publics donateurs, afin de vérifier s'ils ont assuré le suivi de l'exécution des projets financés et s'ils ont bien reçu les rapports financiers, moraux et justificatifs d'exécution des activités avant de verser de nouvelles tranches de financement. Selon les sources d'Hespress, les magistrats de la Cour des comptes se sont concentrés sur la traçabilité des subventions depuis leur versement sur les comptes des associations jusqu'à leur dépense effective, en rapprochant chaque charge des factures et pièces y afférentes, tout en évaluant les réalisations concrètes en contrepartie des fonds publics engagés et en vérifiant le respect des règles comptables et des exigences de gestion des deniers publics. Les prochaines étapes de cet audit devraient trancher sur la nature exacte des dysfonctionnements relevés, une fois finalisées les opérations de recoupement et après réception des clarifications et documents complémentaires demandés aux responsables des associations concernées, permettant ainsi d'établir les infractions avérées et de déterminer les procédures et sanctions applicables à chaque dossier selon les conclusions des audits. The post Faux justificatifs et dépenses floues : Vaste traque aux anomalies comptables dans le secteur associatif appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: «La France est le pays malade de l’Europe» : Sophie Binet fustige le bilan de Macron et le budget 2027
items.description: La secretaire generale de la plus grande confederation syndicale francaise, la Confederation generale du travail (CGT), Sophie Binet, a qualifie la France de « pays malade de l'Europe ». S'exprimant dans une interview accordee a Radio France, elle a souligne que l'Hexagone etait l'un des rares pays a se trouver au bord de la recession. Selon elle, bien que le contexte international ait influence la situation actuelle, la cause principale reside dans la « politique de l'offre mise en place depuis dix ans » par le president francais Emmanuel Macron. Par ailleurs, la secretaire generale de la CGT a critique le projet de budget pour 2027 presente le 17 septembre par le Premier ministre francais Sebastien Lecornu, le qualifiant de « dangereux » et estimant qu'il « sacrifie nos services publics ». Le chef de Matignon a propose de « geler » le budget de l'etat, a l'exception de cinq ministeres, dont celui des Armees, dont le financement sera augmente. Sophie Binet a rappele l'« ete calamiteux » a cause des incendies et de la canicule, et ces catastrophes, selon elle, auraient pu etre evitees « si nos pompiers avaient les moyens » et « si on n'avait pas supprime 45 000 lits dans les hopitaux ». « On est dans une situation ou des millions de travailleurs et travailleuses sont obliges de choisir entre remplir leur caddie ou faire le plein », a-t-elle souligne, precisant que la question « n'est pas de baisser les depenses », mais d'« augmenter les recettes ». Debut septembre, le president du Credit Mutuel Alliance Federale, Daniel Baal, a brosse un tableau sombre de la dette francaise, qu'il a qualifiee d'« inacceptable ». Selon lui, « le seuil d'alerte est atteint depuis un moment, non seulement sur les taux, mais egalement a cause du volume de la dette francaise », et la necessite de la rembourser a des conditions defavorables « rend cette dette encore plus difficilement acceptable ». La dette publique francaise a atteint 117,5 % du PIB a la fin du mois de mars dernier, tandis que le rendement des obligations a dix ans est a son plus haut niveau depuis 2008.

items.title: Mohammed Kudus drops out of Ghana squad for AFCON 2027 qualifiers against Côte d’Ivoire and Gambia
items.description: Mohammed Kudus has opted out of Ghana’s upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia, despite being named in Carlos Queiroz’s 24-man Black Stars squad. Information available to JoySports is that Kudus wants to focus on completing his recovery at Tottenham Hotspur and regaining his best physical condition and form before returning to international action. The decision comes just days after the 26-year-old made his return to Premier League football following a lengthy injury lay-off. We understand the decision has already been communicated to the Ghana Football Association (GFA) and coach Carlos Queiroz. Kudus came off the bench at half-time in Tottenham’s 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday and immediately provided an attacking spark. He set up Conor Gallagher for Tottenham’s first Premier League goal of the season in the 86th minute after cutting the ball back from the byline. The appearance followed his first start since January in Tottenham’s Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool earlier this week. The Ghanaian had been sidelined for seven months after suffering a significant quad injury in January, with Tottenham confirming in April that he had suffered a setback in his recovery and required further specialist assessment. Kudus missed Ghana’s 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign because of the injury. The Ghana Football Association subsequently included him in Queiroz’s latest squad after confirming that he had recovered and returned to competitive football. His last appearance for the Black Stars came on October 12, 2025, when he scored the winning goal in Ghana’s 1-0 World Cup qualifying victory over Comoros in Accra. I survived 3 air crashes for 2027 — Gen. Ijioma
items.description: … APP candidate unveils 23-point manifesto, flags off campaign By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The 2027 governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Party (APP) in Abia State, Major-General Ijioma Nwokoro Ijioma (retd.), has attributed his survival of about 30 road accidents and three air crashes to what he described as a divine purpose to govern the state in 2027. Ijioma spoke on Saturday while formally flagging off his campaign at Umuhu Ezechi Community Primary School, Bende, his country home, after receiving the APP flag from the party’s National Organising Secretary, Mr Obed Agu, who represented the National Chairman, High Chief Uchenna Nnadi. The retired general said one of the air crashes he survived was the incident that claimed the lives of 10 generals, including the former Chief of Army Staff, Lt.-Gen. Andrew Azazi. He recalled that he survived the crash because he had remained at Army Headquarters to prepare the minutes of an earlier engagement instead of joining the flight. “I survived many accidents and escaped three air crashes, including the one that claimed the life of late Chief of Army Staff, Azazi,” he said. “I was the secretary in Army Headquarters that toured everywhere with him. But on that day, after we returned from Ibadan, I was to write the minutes and he said he wanted that minute ready before they returned from Obudu. That was how I stayed back and didn’t die in that air crash that killed 10 Generals. “All these things that have happened and I survived was for one purpose. And that purpose is 2027, when I will take over as the Governor of Abia State.” Ijioma described the APP flag as a responsibility he would not take for granted and pledged to work for the party’s victory in the election. He unveiled a 23-point manifesto covering security, economic development, agriculture, education, energy, infrastructure, culture, accountability and inclusive governance. As part of his economic proposals, Ijioma said his administration would establish 17 local government farms and three state farms, with industries to process agricultural produce. He also proposed the establishment of “Abia rice shops”, “Abia milk shops” and “Abia meat shops”, where residents would be able to purchase locally produced food at subsidised rates. “Anywhere I go, I see hunger on the faces of my people, and I see anger. It is that hunger that I want to feed and remove that anger through responsible leadership, efficient and effective governance,” he said. The APP candidate also promised to establish a 16-storey university building in Umuhu within his first year in office, if elected, and upgrade the Ibere-Umuhu Road. Ijioma promises tougher security measures On insecurity, particularly attacks allegedly linked to herders, Ijioma promised to introduce what he described as an “invisible security fence” across Abia State. He said the proposed security architecture would enable his administration to detect and respond swiftly to security breaches across the state. “Recently, I heard that Fulani herdsmen have started jumping into fences and farms in Ikwuano and other places. When I become the governor of Abia State next year, there will be no issue of Fulani herdsmen everywhere,” he said. “I will build what we call in the military, invisible security fence. And when that is put in place, any breach or insecurity anywhere in Abia within 48 hours will be terminated,” he pledged. He said his proposed security strategy would focus on protecting lives, property, farms and communities, while enabling residents to carry out their activities without fear. Ijioma faults Otti administration Ijioma also criticised the performance of the incumbent Labour Party administration of Governor Alex Otti, questioning aspects of its expenditure, road construction and education programmes. He promised that his administration, if elected, would adopt what he described as a more meticulous approach to public resource management and avoid what he called errors in the presentation of budget performance. “I will be very meticulous and very careful with the management of the resources that will be placed under my care,” he said. The former Director of Military Operations said government performance should be assessed based on what residents could see and experience. He also called for greater accountability in the management of local government funds, alleging that development in some local government areas did not correspond with their increased allocations. Ijioma promises to pursue Kanu’s release On the continued detention of the leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPoB), Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, Ijioma pledged to pursue legal, political and social avenues for his release if elected governor. “I will take every necessary measure, including legal, including political, including social, to compel the Federal Government to release Nnamdi Kanu,” he said. He questioned why Kanu remained in detention while, according to him, some other persons who had been involved in violent activities had subsequently regained their freedom. Ijioma also announced a scholarship covering the education of a Primary Five pupil, Ekene Okorie, up to university level after featuring the boy in a demonstration during his address. Earlier, Agu, who represented the APP national chairman, described Ijioma as a “fearless General” with vast experience and knowledge, expressing confidence in his ability to transform Abia State. The campaign flag-off, described by the party as its first governorship campaign event in the state ahead of the 2027 election, attracted APP candidates, national and state party leaders, and supporters from across Abia. Ijioma, who said his emergence had made history in his community, urged Abians to vote for the APP in the February 6, 2027 governorship election. “This flag that has been presented to me today, I do not take it for granted. I will work assiduously to ensure the victory of this party in the coming election,” he said. The post I survived 3 air crashes for 2027 — Gen. Ijioma appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Packing for a pope: Behind the scenes on foreign trips
items.description: Papal trips mean vast crowds, high-level diplomatic meetings and a formidable amount of behind-the-scenes preparation, from delicately balanced agendas to complex security protection for the head of the Catholic Church. Pope Leo XIV’s visit to France from September 25 to 28, which includes events at the Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Champs-Elysees, will involve some 15,000 members of the security forces. The groundwork for this visit — the first papal trip to Paris since 2008 — was laid well before it was officially announced. A crowd awaits Pope Leo XIV’s address from the window of the apostolic palace overlooking St Peter’s Square during his Sunday Angelus prayer at the Vatican on September 20, 2026. —AFP Countries invite the pope, but whether or not he visits is based on a range of pastoral and political considerations. The complex decision “depends heavily on the international context”, a Vatican source told AFP . The Vatican takes into account social and political circumstances, from conflicts to humanitarian crises, as well as the situation of the local church and the history of previous visits. But each pope has his own wish list and the choice of destinations also reflects the papacy’s geopolitical priorities. For example, “John Paul II travelled extensively to eastern European countries to denounce Communism,” the source said. A cyclist rides past a grandstand under construction at Place de la Concorde, with the Obelisk and the Eiffel Tower in the background, in Paris on September 16, 2026, ahead of the visit of Pope Leo XIV to France. — AFP In his 12 years as pontiff, the Argentinian Pope Francis favoured the “peripheries” of the Church, from Iraq to Mongolia and Papua New Guinea, while US-born Leo seems more inclined towards Europe and major international institutions. Sky-high briefing Since the Vatican does not have an official aircraft, the Holy See charters a commercial plane from Italian national airline ITA for the outbound journey, while the return flight is generally operated by the host country. On board, the pope occupies seat 1A, at the front left of the cabin. In front of him is a depiction of the Virgin Mary. Beside him, in seats bearing the Holy See coat of arms, sit cardinals, his private secretaries, and a doctor. Dressed in dark suits and ties, some 40 officers from the Vatican Gendarmerie and Swiss Guard provide close protection. In the rear of the cabin travel the media: approximately 80 journalists, photographers and cameramen. Media outlets pay for their correspondents’ tickets, which generally cost several thousand euros. On the outbound journey, the pope walks down the plane, greeting the journalists individually. He sometimes shares a few personal anecdotes and some correspondents give him presents — from football shirts to food. Nuns hold a banner reading the name of their insitute before, as they await Pope Leo XIV’s address from the window of the apostolic palace overlooking St Peter’s Square during his Sunday Angelus prayer at the Vatican on September 20. — AFP On the return trip, the pontiff holds one of the most closely watched press conferences in the world: a sky-high briefing at 10,000 metres in a cabin cluttered with cameras, microphones and tripods. The luggage includes the pope’s personal belongings, speeches prepared weeks in advance, and security equipment. There are also sealed cases containing liturgical objects — such as chasubles, to be worn during mass — and dozens of official gifts for heads of state and dignitaries, such as paintings, books or rosaries. ‘Advance team’ Security and logistics are the biggest challenges. With his dual status as head of state and leader of 1.4 billion Catholics, the pope is one of the most heavily protected figures in the world. The medical team carries a supply of the pope’s blood type, while a hospital suite is kept on standby in the host country. The iconic white pope-mobile is transported in advance, and a backup vehicle is ready on site. Journalists, including AFP, precede the pope at every stage in a convoy escorted by law enforcement, with sirens blaring. As before each trip, a Vatican delegation known as the “advance team” travelled to France in mid-July to finalise the details with local authorities. “The programme can change at the very last minute,” a Vatican security source told AFP . “Everything has to be meticulously planned, almost down to the second.”

items.title: Shettima leads Nigeria’s delegation to 81st UNGA
items.description: —Govs Fubara, Dauda Lawal, ministers, senior officials join delegation to New York By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA —THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima will lead Nigeria’s delegation to the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, UNGA, in New York, United States. A statement by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communication, Office of the Vice President, Stanley Nkwocha, stated that President Bola Tinubu mandated Senator Shettima to represent him at the event. VP Shettima will lead a high-level delegation comprising Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State; Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State; ministers and other senior government officials. The 81st UNGA General Debate will hold from September 22 to 28, 2026, under the theme, “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.” At the General Debate, Senator Shettima will deliver Nigeria’s national statement, outlining the country’s position and priorities on major global issues with implications for national development, peace and security, economic growth and international cooperation. The Vice President will also participate in high-level meetings during the UNGA week, including engagements on the Right to Development, climate action and other issues of strategic importance to Nigeria and the African continent. Senator Shettima is also expected to join other world leaders at the traditional reception for Heads of Delegation and participate in a series of bilateral meetings with leaders of other countries, international organisations and development partners on the sidelines of the General Assembly. The engagements will provide Nigeria an opportunity to advance President Tinubu’s economic diplomacy, deepen strategic partnerships and strengthen the country’s voice on reform of the global financial architecture, sustainable development, climate finance and multilateral cooperation. VP Shettima will return to Nigeria at the conclusion of his engagements in New York. The post Shettima leads Nigeria’s delegation to 81st UNGA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Vers un retour de la conscription ? L'Allemagne rend obligatoire la visite médicale pour les jeunes hommes, même ceux qui refusent l'armée
items.description: Les forces armees allemandes ont commence a proceder a des examens medicaux obligatoires pour les hommes de 18 ans, meme si ceux-ci ont indique dans leur questionnaire qu'ils ne souhaitaient pas effectuer leur service militaire, a rapporte le 19 septembre le Berliner Morgenpost en se referant a un rapport du ministere federal allemand de la Defense sur l'evolution des effectifs. Selon ce dernier, pres d'un millier d'hommes nes en 2008, ayant clairement indique dans leur questionnaire leur desinteret pour le service militaire, ont subi cet examen depuis juillet. Il est prevu d'augmenter progressivement le nombre de ces examens. Le Berliner Morgenpost a note qu'une visite medicale obligatoire a grande echelle pour tous les hommes de cette tranche d'âge devrait debuter en juillet 2027. D'ici la, la Bundeswehr a l'intention de mettre en place 24 centres specialises dans tout le pays. Le ministere allemand de la Defense assure toutefois que le fait de se presenter a cette visite medicale n'entraîne pas la conscription : la nouvelle forme de service militaire reste pour l'instant volontaire. Par ailleurs, depuis le debut de l'annee 2026, le Bundeswehr envoie a tous les citoyens allemands âges de 18 ans des questionnaires portant sur leur sante, leur formation et leur disposition a servir. Les hommes sont tenus de les remplir, tandis que les femmes ne sont pas obligees de le faire. Fin août, environ 96 % des hommes avaient repondu, contre seulement 3,5 % des femmes. Une militarisation qui inquiete meme les voisins La tendance militariste des autorites allemandes se manifeste de plus en plus ouvertement ces derniers temps. En avril dernier, le ministre-president de Baviere, Markus Soder, a estime que l'Allemagne devait retablir le service militaire obligatoire des que possible, car le pays ne pourrait pas assurer suffisamment sa securite si l'armee ne comptait que des volontaires. a la meme epoque, le ministre allemand de la Defense, Boris Pistorius, a presente la strategie militaire de la Bundeswehr, qui vise a faire des forces armees allemandes l'armee la plus puissante d'Europe. Ce document preconisait notamment d'augmenter les effectifs des forces armees allemandes, reservistes compris, pour atteindre au moins 460 000 personnes, tout en evoquant une « menace » emanant de la Russie. Le renforcement rapide de la puissance militaire allemande a deja commence a inquieter d'autres pays europeens. Selon le Wall Street Journal , depuis que le president americain Donald Trump a appele Berlin a augmenter ses depenses de defense, le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz, le dirigeant deja le moins populaire du pays , a decide de consacrer des milliards de dollars a ces fins. En consequence, les responsables europeens ont commence a craindre qu'un tel renforcement de la puissance militaire de l'Allemagne ne vienne modifier l'equilibre des forces sur le continent. La Russie rejette l'idee d'une menace pour l'Europe, tout en restant vigilante Le 16 septembre, Ioulia Zhdanova, representante de la Russie aux negociations de Vienne sur la securite militaire et le controle des armements, a condamne la politique du gouvernement allemand visant a se preparer a un eventuel conflit de grande ampleur avec la Russie. Selon elle, la mise en place d'une organisation militaire du pays se traduit par la preparation des infrastructures militaires et logistiques, voire du systeme de sante. Moscou rejette toutefois les allegations infondees de l'Occident concernant une pretendue attaque russe contre les pays de l'OTAN. Le president russe Vladimir Poutine a affirme que la Russie n'avait aucune raison geopolitique, economique ou militaire d'entrer en guerre contre l'Alliance, et a qualifie d' « absurdite » l'hypothese d'une attaque de la Russie contre l'OTAN. La Russie reste neanmoins vigilante, mettant en garde les pays europeens contre toute action militaire a son encontre. Le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Sergueï Lavrov, a ainsi averti que si l'Europe attaquait la Russie, « ce sera une tout autre guerre, et elle sera tres courte ».

items.title: Boulgou/Niaogho : Les appelés de l’immersion patriotique en excursion culturelle de 48 heures au musée Doleema
items.description: Boulgou/Niaogho : Les appelés de l'immersion patriotique en excursion culturelle de 48 heures au musée Doleema Niaogho, 20 septembre 2026 (AIB)-Le Secrétaire général de la commune de Niaogho, le camarade Ambroise Bayili, a présidé, le vendredi 18 septembre 2026, la cérémonie d'ouverture des 48 heures d'excursion culturelle et citoyenne des appelés à l'immersion patriotique, au musée Doleema de Niaogho. Dans son allocution, le Secrétaire général a salué une initiative qu'il a jugée porteuse de sens. Il a souligné que la culture demeure le socle du devenir d'un peuple et a invité les jeunes à s'approprier les valeurs cardinales de notre société pour bâtir le développement de la Nation. Il a, par ailleurs, exprimé sa gratitude au parrain de l'événement et au promoteur du musée pour leur accompagnement. Le parrain de cette édition, le Directeur général de Global Services Company, le camarade Édouard Soubeiga, s'est dit honoré de soutenir cette incursion citoyenne et culturelle. « Cette initiative revêt une importance particulière, car elle permet à notre jeunesse de se rapprocher de son histoire, de ses racines et de son patrimoine », a-t-il affirmé. Le camarade Soubeiga a réaffirmé son engagement à soutenir la jeunesse et a invité le secteur privé à s'investir davantage dans les actions citoyennes. Il a souligné que cette dynamique s'inscrit dans la vision du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, qui œuvre pour une véritable indépendance et un développement souverain du Burkina Faso. Pour le responsable des appelés, le camarade Matirou, cette immersion au musée vise l'appropriation des valeurs culturelles fondamentales, en complément des notions de civisme, de patriotisme et de discipline acquises lors de leur formation à Tenkodogo. « En tant que jeunes représentant l'avenir du pays, nous devons incarner ces principes », a-t-il soutenu. Au programme de ces 48 heures, trois communications majeures sont prévues : « Connaître son pays, aimer son peuple, servir sa Nation » ; « Le peuple Bissa : histoire et patrimoine culturel » ; « Rôle de la jeune burkinabè dans le développement de sa commune ». items.title: Décès de Sid Ahmed Agoumi : Tebboune rend hommage à un « ami de grande stature »
items.description: L’acteur et dramaturge algérien Sid Ahmed Agoumi est décédé ce dimanche 20 septembre à l’âge de 86 ans. L’annonce de sa disparition a été suivie d’une pluie de messages de condoléances et d’hommages. Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a exprimé sa tristesse à la suite du « notre cher ami, feu l'artiste Ahmed Meziane (Sid Ahmed Agoumi). » « Nous partageons votre douleur, ainsi que celle des artistes, des intellectuels et de son vaste public d'admirateurs, pour l'une des figures les plus célèbres et les plus distinguées dont la contribution artistique a marqué pendant des décennies le paysage culturel et artistique de notre pays », a écrit Abdelmadjid Tebboune dans l’hommage qu’il a rendu à ce célèbre acteur qui a joué dans de nombreux films algériens. Le président de la République a rendu hommage à un « acteur talentueux et à un intellectuel cultivé, passionné par la culture nationale et l'authenticité de l'art algérien » Décès de Sid Ahmed Agoumi : Tebboune exprime sa tristesse à la suite de la perte d’un ami Né en octobre 1940 à Alger, Sid Ahmed Agoumi a marqué de son « empreinte plus de 50 films et productions télévisées, tant au niveau national qu'international, et a brillé par un remarquable professionnalisme dans des films acclamés tels que « Z » et « Chronique des années de braises », a ajouté M. Tebboune. Le Président partage avec la famille du défunt la « peine et le chagrin causés par la perte d'une figure dont les créations théâtrales et cinématographiques ont marqué des générations depuis les années 1960 ». « J’ai personnellement connu Sid Ahmed Agoumi comme un homme d'une grande stature, un ami doté d'un sens patriotique et humain élevé », a témoigné Abdelmadjid Tebboune. L’article Décès de Sid Ahmed Agoumi : Tebboune rend hommage à un « ami de grande stature » est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Anambra police arrest woman over alleged self-kidnap
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Anambra State Police Command has arrested a 22-year-old woman, Nwachukwu Chidubem Blessing, over an alleged case of conspiracy, fraud and self-kidnapping. The suspect was arrested by operatives of the Rapid Response Squad (RRS), Awkuzu, following intelligence gathered during an investigation into her alleged abduction. The state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, said the woman was reportedly abducted along the Onitsha–Asaba Expressway on August 29, 2026. He said her family subsequently paid N3 million in ransom, but the woman was allegedly not released, prompting further investigation by the police. Ikenga said sustained intelligence gathering and investigative efforts led police operatives to a room in Asaba, Delta State, where the alleged victim was found and recovered on September 18. “Preliminary findings from the investigation indicate that the lady allegedly conspired with a female associate identified as Onyinye, whose other names are yet to be established, and another male accomplice, whose identity is presently unknown, to stage her own kidnapping and obtain money from her family,” Ikenga said. He said the arrested woman was assisting the police with information that could help establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify and apprehend her alleged accomplices. Ikenga added that the Anambra State Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Amah, had directed that the investigation be intensified to unravel the circumstances surrounding the case. He said anyone found culpable would be brought to justice in accordance with the law. The post Anambra police arrest woman over alleged self-kidnap appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CNG buses not enough to tame transport crisis, HURIWA tells FG
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria, HURIWA, has urged the Federal Government to complement its Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, transportation initiative with measures to reduce the cost of petrol and other energy inputs driving transportation and production costs across the country. HURIWA said the Federal Government’s directive to state governors to reduce transportation fares through expanded CNG and electric-powered public transportation programmes could provide relief for commuters, but should not be treated as a substitute for broader measures to address high energy costs. In a press statement by its National Coordinator, Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, yesterday, the organisation called for greater transparency in the pricing of petrol and measures capable of making energy costs more affordable for households and businesses. It also urged the Federal Government to consider measures that could move petrol prices towards the levels recorded before the current period of elevated fuel costs, while taking into account the fiscal implications of any intervention. The call followed President Bola Tinubu’s directive to the 36 state governors to ensure measurable reductions in transportation costs from October 1 through expanded CNG and electric-powered public transportation programmes. HURIWA said cheaper-energy buses could help reduce fares on routes where they operate, but argued that high energy and transportation costs also affect manufacturing, agriculture, food distribution, logistics, construction and small businesses. According to the group, increases in transportation and energy costs are ultimately reflected in the prices of goods and services. It therefore urged the Federal Government to pursue a broader energy-cost reduction strategy alongside the CNG initiative. HURIWA said state governments could provide transportation interventions but could not independently address all the structural factors affecting fuel prices and the wider downstream petroleum sector. The organisation urged the Federal Government to explore fiscal, regulatory and market-based measures capable of stabilising energy costs without returning to a subsidy regime that could impose unsustainable pressure on public finances. It also called for greater transparency in the petrol pricing structure, including the components relating to crude oil, refining, importation, transportation, margins, taxes and other applicable charges. “Nigerians deserve to understand the factors determining the price they pay at the pump and the measures being taken to make energy more affordable,” HURIWA said. The group welcomed the expansion of CNG conversion centres and alternative-energy transportation, but said the initiative should form part of a wider economic strategy. It noted that reducing transportation costs alone would not address the pressures facing manufacturers, farmers, traders and households from high energy and logistics costs. HURIWA expressed particular concern over the impact of persistent energy costs on manufacturers, saying businesses facing rising production and logistics expenses could be forced to scale down operations, increase prices or suspend production. It consequently urged the Federal Government to accelerate efforts to expand domestic refining capacity, promote competition in the downstream petroleum sector and introduce targeted measures to reduce energy costs for manufacturers, farmers, transport operators and households. The organisation also appealed to state governments implementing transportation interventions to ensure that the benefits reach commuters and are accompanied by transparent monitoring. HURIWA called for consultations involving the Federal Government, state governments, labour, manufacturers, transport operators and civil society organisations on measures to reduce energy and transportation costs. It said the objective should be to improve household purchasing power, support domestic production and make transportation more affordable. “CNG is part of the solution, but it should be complemented by broader measures to address the factors driving energy and transportation costs,” the group said. The post CNG buses not enough to tame transport crisis, HURIWA tells FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

South-East Speakers seek uniform legislative standards
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Speakers of the South-East Houses of Assembly have agreed to strengthen collaboration among the five legislatures to promote standardised procedures and uniform legislative best practices across the zone. The speakers made the commitment at a meeting in Awka, where they also stressed the need to redefine inter-state legislative cooperation to address common challenges confronting the South-East. They identified effective policing, good governance, economic opportunities, justice and strong institutions as critical components of sustainable security and development in the region. The host Speaker and Vice Chairman of the South-East Conference of Speakers, Dr Somtochukwu Udeze of the Anambra State House of Assembly, said the region had demonstrated considerable individual capacity but needed to translate such capacity into durable institutions and coordinated regional action. Udeze urged his colleagues to move beyond resolutions and identify specific areas of legislation for comparative review. “Let us select areas for possible model legislation. Let us establish a mechanism for continuous engagement among the five Houses. Let us assign responsibility and timelines,” he said. He said the objective should be to develop a practical roadmap for legislative cooperation, stressing that laws enacted by the Houses must withstand constitutional scrutiny, administrative realities and the test of time. “If the five Houses can raise the standard of their legislative work, learn systematically from one another and build a working relationship around the common interests of our people, we will have done something that extends beyond the life of any individual Assembly. That, ultimately, is the value of institutional reform,” Udeze said. He maintained that political differences should not prevent institutional cooperation among the states. “We should be able to disagree politically and still cooperate institutionally. We should be able to maintain the autonomy of our five Houses while developing common standards. We should be able to compete for investment while removing unnecessary regulatory barriers between our states,” he said. Udeze said the quality of legislation had a significant impact on the quality of administration, noting that unclear laws could create uncertainty and weak procedures could undermine effective governance. He said the proposed standardisation should go beyond the Standing Orders and procedures governing plenary sessions. “This is why I believe the conversation about standardising legislative procedures in the South-East should go beyond Standing Orders and the mechanics of how we conduct plenary,” he said. Udeze proposed the establishment of a platform through which the five Houses could continuously compare legislation, exchange legislative research, examine emerging regional issues and develop model legislative provisions where necessary. He also advocated a shift from periodic political consultations among the states to structured institutional cooperation. “The Governors have their own forum and constitutional responsibilities. We, as legislators, can have ours,” he said. According to him, the proposed mechanism should be professional and capable of surviving changes in government and political parties. He suggested that it could maintain a comparative database of major laws passed by the five Houses, identify obsolete, conflicting or duplicative provisions, develop model Bills where regional consistency was desirable, organise continuing training for legislators and legislative staff, and facilitate joint committee-level consideration of issues with cross-state implications. In a communique issued after the meeting, the speakers in attendance commended the five South-East governors for what they described as developmental strides in their respective states. They also pledged continued legislative partnership in support of good governance and regional development. The four Speakers who attended the meeting were Udeze of Anambra State, Emmanuel Emeruwa of Abia State, Moses Ije Odunwa of Ebonyi State and Uche Ugwu of Enugu State. The post South-East Speakers seek uniform legislative standards appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Maroc : découverte d’un complexe agricole vieux de 5 000 ans et d’une fortification préhistorique inédite
items.description: Le site d'Oued Beht, dans la province de Khemisset, s'impose comme un site majeur pour comprendre les societes prehistoriques du Maghreb. Les nouvelles recherches menees par une equipe internationale ont permis de documenter a la fois une importante societe agricole du Neolithique final et un systeme defensif datant de plusieurs millenaires. Les resultats, issus notamment de la troisieme campagne de fouilles de l'Oued Beht Archaeological Project, menee en 2023, ont ete publies en septembre 2026 dans la revue Libyan Studies , editee par Cambridge University Press. Le projet associe notamment des chercheurs marocains, britanniques et italiens. Une societe agricole de grande ampleur Les recherches precedentes avaient deja revele a Oued Beht une societe agricole jusque-la inconnue, active entre environ 3 400 et 2 900 avant notre ere. Les vestiges s'etendent sur pres de 9 a 10 hectares, faisant du site le plus vaste complexe agricole connu en Afrique au-dela de la vallee du Nil pour cette periode. Les fouilles ont notamment livre des traces de cultures et d'elevage, ainsi qu'une importante quantite de materiel archeologique, dont des outils en pierre et des poteries. Ces decouvertes temoignent d'une societe deja structuree et engagee dans des activites agricoles et artisanales diversifiees. Les chercheurs soulignent egalement des similitudes avec certaines evolutions contemporaines observees dans la peninsule Iberique, suggerant que le nord-ouest de l'Afrique participait aux dynamiques d'echanges et d'interactions de la Mediterranee occidentale prehistorique. Un systeme defensif vieux de 3 500 a 4 000 ans La troisieme campagne de fouilles a egalement permis de resoudre une enigme archeologique vieille de plusieurs decennies. Des structures reperees des les annees 1930 sur une crete du site ont ete identifiees comme faisant partie d'un systeme defensif compose notamment d'un large fosse et d'un rempart en terre. Les datations au radiocarbone situent sa construction entre environ 4 000 et 3 500 ans, soit au debut et au milieu du IIe millenaire avant notre ere. Il s'agit, selon les chercheurs, du plus ancien systeme defensif documente en Afrique du Nord hors de la vallee du Nil. Le dispositif profitait de la topographie naturelle de la crete pour controler l'acces a la partie meridionale du site. Sa construction implique une capacite a mobiliser et coordonner une main-d'œuvre importante, meme si les chercheurs ne peuvent pas encore determiner avec certitude sa fonction exacte : defense contre des attaques, controle des deplacements ou protection de ressources et de terres. Un site occupe pendant plusieurs millenaires Oued Beht temoigne ainsi d'une occupation et d'une transformation du paysage sur une tres longue periode. Apres les occupations prehistoriques, le site a notamment connu une nouvelle phase d'utilisation au Moyen Âge, avec des structures et des amenagements datant de cette periode. Pour les archeologues, ces decouvertes contribuent a reevaluer la place du Maghreb dans l'histoire des societes complexes de la Mediterranee occidentale. Elles apportent notamment de nouvelles donnees sur une periode de la prehistoire nord-africaine longtemps moins documentee que celle de la peninsule Iberique ou de la Mediterranee orientale.

items.title: Six die, two injured in Kogi road crash
items.description: KABBA — Six persons have been killed and two others injured in a road crash along the Kabba-Odo-Ape Road in Kabba-Bunu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Kogi Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Mr Lawal Fagge, confirmed the incident in a telephone interview on Sunday. Fagge said the crash, which occurred on Saturday afternoon, involved a truck and a commercial vehicle. He attributed the accident to speeding, adding that residents of Odo-Ape assisted in rescuing the survivors. “It is unfortunate that six persons lost their lives, while two others sustained varying degrees of injuries as a result of the tragic incident involving a truck and another vehicle along the Kabba-Odo-Ape Road,” he said. The sector commander urged motorists to avoid speeding and unnecessary overtaking, and to desist from driving when fatigued. “We will continue to advise motorists to avoid speeding, unnecessary overtaking and desist from driving while fatigued. This is very important in preventing road crashes,” he said. Fagge said the bodies of the deceased had been deposited at the morgue of the General Hospital, Kabba. (NAN) The post Six die, two injured in Kogi road crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel
items.description: The United States on Sunday warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthis could “escalate rapidly” after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. “This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly,” the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”. US President Donald Trump also cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday. The White House gave no explanation for the early return, which comes as a new threshold was crossed in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and are fighting government forces backed by a coalition. Loud explosions rang out on Saturday in the Saudi capital, where AFP journalists saw a fuel tank bearing the logo of oil giant Aramco on fire near the airport. In recent weeks, the Houthis’ lightning offensive seizing swathes of Yemeni territory has left hundreds dead and, according to the UN refugee agency, displaced more than 110,000 people. The violence has already disrupted exports from Saudi Arabia , the world’s leading supplier of crude oil, as well as maritime traffic. CIA chief meets Egypt’s Sisi On Sunday, US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Director John Ratcliffe met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in a rare visit to Cairo. Sisi stressed “the paramount importance of settling regional crises through political and diplomatic tracks”, according to a presidency statement. The visit came days after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was also in the Egyptian capital , where he and Sisi urged safe and secure navigation through Bab al-Mandab, after the Houthis seized the Yemeni coast. The Bab al-Mandab strait is a Red Sea waterway that is crucial to energy flows and global shipping and which has become even more strategic since Iran imposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. Condemning the Houthis’ latest attacks, Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told the broadcaster NTV that his country had had discussions with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, partners in a mutual defence pact, about possible assistance. “In this regard, military needs, especially in state technical matters, may happen. There would be no problem in meeting this demand either,” he said. Saudi Arabia meanwhile seemed to contain the fallout of the Houthis’ attacks on its territory. On Sunday, the attack on Riyadh was not mentioned in several major Saudi papers, even though hours beforehand, the Saudi-led coalition had said that a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis was “successfully intercepted and destroyed”. The coalition added that the pro-Iranian fighters had tried to target “civilians and civilian infrastructure” in several cities in the west of the kingdom, including the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, an important export hub for Saudi oil. It said these attacks were thwarted by the Gulf monarchy’s air defences. Claiming responsibility for the attack, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said fighters had carried out “two successful military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones”. “The first targeted sensitive sites in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu.” Saudi Arabia has responded with scores of airstrikes on Houthi-held areas but has been unable to stop the fighters’ advance. The United States, according to US news platform Axios , last week refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis, but Washington has since approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets. Widening conflict This is the first time since Yemen’s civil war resumed that strikes have threatened the Saudi capital, piling further pressure on a global economy already rocked by seven months of war between the US and Iran. Iran’s top negotiator said Tehran had conveyed to the US through mediators its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which it has blockaded throughout the Middle East war. The Middle East war began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran , which responded with retaliatory attacks on nearby Gulf countries. Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen also carried out attacks against their foes. While conflict in Yemen predates the Middle East war, the recent escalation in the country — one of the world’s poorest — has turned it into the most active front of the wider violence. A fragile truce reached in 2022 collapsed in July, and the Houthis went on an all-out offensive against the internationally recognised government this month.

items.title: 200 nights on the streets
Les Lionceaux visent un triplé historique
items.description: Vainqueur des deux dernières éditions du tournoi Ufoa-A U17, le Sénégal dispute une nouvelle finale ce dimanche 20 septembre 2026, au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor de Dakar, face à la Gambie, qui a battu le Libéria (2-1). Les Lionceaux tenteront de décrocher un troisième trophée consécutif, une performance encore jamais réalisée dans la zone. L’équipe nationale U17 du Sénégal est à 90 minutes d’un nouveau sacre. Après leur large victoire contre la Guinée en demi-finale (3-0), les jeunes Sénégalais ont atteint leur premier objectif : se qualifier pour la finale et assurer leur participation à la prochaine Can U17, prévue au Maroc, où ils pourront défendre leur titre. Il reste désormais à remporter la finale. Le Sénégal a remporté les deux précédentes éditions. En octobre 2025, grâce à un doublé de Souleymane Commissaire Faye, toujours présent, il avait dominé le Mali (2-0) en finale à Bamako. En novembre 2024, à Dakar, il avait déjà pris le dessus sur les Aiglons (3-3, 5-4 aux tirs au but). Cette fois, la Gambie se dresse sur la route des Lionceaux. Les deux équipes se connaissent bien. En phase de poules, elles s’étaient quittées sur un nul vierge (0-0). Cette fois, un vainqueur devra être désigné. Invaincu depuis le début du tournoi, le Sénégal a largement dominé la Mauritanie (4-0) et la Sierra Leone (5-0), avant de battre la Guinée en demi-finale. En cas de succès dimanche, les hommes de Lamine Sané deviendraient la première équipe à remporter trois finales Ufoa-A U17 consécutives. Mais la Gambie affiche également de solides arguments. Les Young Scorpions ont battu la Sierra Leone (4-1), la Mauritanie (3-1), puis le Libéria (2-1) en demi-finale. Invaincus eux aussi, ils ont inscrit 9 buts pour seulement 3 encaissés, avec pour seul accroc le nul face au Sénégal en phase de groupes. En finale, ils tenteront d’inscrire leur pays au palmarès de la compétition. Le Sénégal possède toutefois la meilleure attaque et la meilleure défense du tournoi, avec 12 buts marqués et aucun encaissé. Pour soulever à nouveau le trophée Ufoa ce dimanche, les Lionceaux devront conserver leur solidité défensive et leur efficacité offensive face aux Young Scorpions. Julien Mbesse SÈNE

items.title: Why NCAA needs research unit to guide aviation policy – Aligbe
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Former General Manager, Public Affairs of Nigerian Airways, Mr Chris Aligbe, has urged the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to establish a research and development unit to provide data-driven solutions to challenges confronting the aviation sector and guide policy decisions. Aligbe, now the Chief Executive Officer of Belujane Konzult, lamented the absence of a research and development structure within the industry, saying it had contributed to poor policy decisions, particularly in route planning, airline operations and revenue generation. He spoke at the 30th Annual Conference of the League of Airport and Aviation Correspondents, LAAC, themed ‘Towards Sustainable Aviation Industry: Balancing Government Revenue Demands with Sector Growth,’ held in Lagos. His words: “I think one of the big problems we have in the industry is that there is no section, even within the airlines or the agencies, particularly the NCAA, that is a regulator, that has a research and development unit. We need that in the industry because when airlines want to go to Abuja, for instance, the NCAA will say: ‘sorry, this is what has happened over the years. We cannot allow you to go there because you will fly empty or you’ll come back and start having problems’. “The same thing in the West Coast. I keep complaining. I am not against any airline, but I feel pain. When a small airline will come and fly 27 weekly frequencies into Nigeria to a place where Nigerians are not going directly, they are carrying our airlines, our passengers to that place and flying them out. “It is painful. That’s why sometimes I complain vehemently. And the killer airlines, killer bugs are coming, the sub-regional airlines. They are not going to survive for a long time because their vision is part political and others, except maybe one or two of them. But they will undermine the bigger airlines that have been there. And when they undermine them, eventually they will die, like bugs, but they would have killed the others. “That’s why we need research departments to be able to achieve some of these things, and improve the revenue situation. We should also be able to review the policy and revenue policy in the industry every five years.” The post Why NCAA needs research unit to guide aviation policy – Aligbe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mambilla: APC’s claims long on propaganda, short on evidence – Paul Ibe
items.description: By Paul Ibe The APC Presidential Campaign Council wants Nigerians to believe that the Mambilla arbitration delivered a corruption verdict against Atiku Abubakar. It did not. The tribunal examined a $500,000 transfer made on 30 January 2003 by Sunrise promoter Leno Adesanya, through China Castle Investments Limited, to the US bank account of Jennifer Douglas, then Atiku’s wife. The tribunal did not accept Adesanya’s explanation that the payment represented a foreign-exchange transaction conducted for Atiku. It found that the explanation was unsupported by contemporaneous documentary evidence and regarded the circumstances surrounding the payment as raising “red flags”. Those are legitimate matters for scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a conviction and “red flags” are not proof of a corrupt quid pro quo. And, crucially, they are not a finding that Atiku used his office to procure the Mambilla contract. The disputed award letter was issued on 22 May 2003 by then Minister of Power and Steel, Olu Agunloye. The controversy before the tribunal included whether the purported award had the necessary presidential and Federal Executive Council authority. Published accounts of the award show that President Olusegun Obasanjo had directed that the matter be presented to the Federal Executive Council, while the extent of any subsequent approval became a central issue in the arbitration. Yet the APC Presidential Campaign Council rushed from those facts to dramatic accusations of “treasonable act”, “greed”, “bribe”, “corruption” and an “illegal contract”. The obvious questions therefore remain. Where is the evidence that Atiku instructed Agunloye to issue the disputed award? Where is the directive showing that Atiku circumvented President Obasanjo or the Federal Executive Council? Where is the evidence establishing that the $500,000 payment was consideration for an official act performed by Atiku? Most importantly, where is the tribunal’s finding that Atiku actually exercised his office to procure Sunrise’s award? The tribunal did conclude that Atiku possessed a considerable degree of power and influence within the Federal Government during the first half of 2003. It also examined his involvement in discussions surrounding the Mambilla project. But published accounts of the award state that the tribunal did not arrive at the conclusion that he actually exercised his official duties in a manner that fostered the award to Sunrise. That distinction is fundamental. Political influence is not, by itself, proof of corruption. Participation in government discussions is not proof of corruption. A suspicious or unexplained financial transaction can justify investigation and questions, but it does not automatically prove a corrupt bargain. Nor should another basic fact be obscured: the proceeding was an international commercial arbitration between Sunrise and the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Atiku was not a party to that arbitration and did not testify before the tribunal. The APC is entitled to interrogate Atiku’s record and to demand explanations concerning the $500,000 transaction. What it should not do is transform suspicion, adverse inferences and “red flags” into a corruption finding against Atiku that the tribunal itself did not make. If the APC Presidential Campaign Council maintains that Atiku corruptly procured the Mambilla contract, it should identify the evidence connecting him directly to the disputed award: a directive, correspondence, instruction, testimony or other record showing that he used his office to secure the contract for Sunrise. Politics does not lower the burden of evidence. There is a difference between a suspicious circumstance and proof; between an allegation and a finding; and between political propaganda and the actual record of a tribunal. On Mambilla, the APC Presidential Campaign Council has made claims that go further than the findings publicly reported from the arbitration. That is the problem with its case: long on political propaganda, short on evidence. Paul Ibe, Media Adviser to Atiku Abubakar, writes from Abuja The post Mambilla: APC’s claims long on propaganda, short on evidence – Paul Ibe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Real Cost of Delayed Chemical Shipments: How Logistics Affect Industrial Procurement
items.description: For industrial buyers, the cost of a chemical shipment is not limited to the price per ton. Delivery time, freight, documentation, packaging, and route selection can all affect the final cost. This is why chemical shipment delays can create problems that are much more expensive than the original difference between two supplier quotations. A shipment that arrives a few days late may seem manageable. But for a factory or distributor working with tight production schedules, even a short delay can affect inventory, production, and customer deliveries.

items.description: Burkina-Bazèga-Ressources-Animales-Campagne-Vaccination Burkina: plus de 2 milliards FCFA mobilisés par le gouvernement en faveur de la santé animale Kombissiri, 20 sept.2026(AIB)-Plus de 2 milliards de francs CFA seront mobilisés pour les campagnes nationales de vaccination, de déparasitage, d'insémination artificielle et de digitalisation de l'identification des animaux d'élevage, dont le lancement a eu lieu samedi, à Kombissiri sous la présidence du ministre d'État, ministre chargé des ressources animales et halieutiques, Commandant Ismaël Sombié. La commune de Kombissiri, dans la province du Bazèga, région du Nazinon, a abrité la cérémonie nationale de lancement conjoint des campagnes de vaccination, de déparasitage, d'insémination artificielle et de digitalisation de l'identification des animaux, présidée par le ministre d'État, ministre en charge des ressources animales et halieutiques, camarade Commandant Ismaël Sombié. Cette cérémonie s'inscrit dans le cadre de l'offensive agropastorale, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028. Pour le directeur général des services vétérinaires, responsable du programme budgétaire 082, camarade Vétérinaire Capitaine Aboubacar Nacro, ces campagnes visent la protection sanitaire du cheptel, l'amélioration de son potentiel génétique et une meilleure maîtrise de la mobilité des animaux. Selon camarade Nacro, des efforts importants sont consentis par l'État du Burkina Faso en matière de subvention des prix des intrants vétérinaires, notamment les vaccins, les déparasitants et les semences animales, avec la gratuité pour la majorité des vaccins, afin d'en faciliter l'accès aux braves producteurs. L'intensification des campagnes de vaccination a permis de passer de quatre (04) maladies couvertes en 2022 à dix (10) maladies en 2025, en prenant en compte la vaccination des poissons. Selon le ministre délégué chargé des ressources animales, camarade Amadou Dicko, plusieurs millions d'animaux sont concernés, soit plus de 18 millions de volailles, 5 millions de bovins et plus de 5 millions de petits ruminants. Pour l'insémination artificielle, ce sont plus de 100 mille bovins et 15 mille truies qui sont concernés. Pour cette campagne, plus de 300 mille bovins seront identifiés à l'aide d'outils électroniques qui permettront de reconnaître les animaux volés, de retrouver les troupeaux perdus, ainsi que d'identifier leurs propriétaires. « L'ensemble des opérations d'insémination, de vaccination et d'identification des animaux coûtera au budget national, pour cette campagne 2026-2027, autour de 2 milliards de francs CFA », a précisé camarade Dicko. À Kombissiri, la cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par des actes d'insémination artificielle des vaches, de vaccination et d'identification d'animaux, ainsi que par la remise symbolique de matériel d'insémination artificielle et de vaccination à la direction régionale en charge des ressources animales et halieutiques du Nazinon. Le ministre d'État, ministre chargé des ressources animales et halieutiques, camarade Commandant Ismaël Sombié, a invité les producteurs fortement mobilisés à respecter les décisions prises par le Gouvernement quant à la vente des animaux. Pour le Camarade Sombié, au regard des sacrifices consentis par l'Etat, les producteurs doivent privilégier les consommateurs nationaux. Au regard des moyens mis au profit des ressources animales, camarade Vétérinaire Capitaine Aboubacar Nacro a invité les éleveurs à saisir les opportunités offertes par ces campagnes pour protéger leurs animaux, améliorer leur productivité et participer ainsi à l'effort national pour l'atteinte de la souveraineté animalière. Agence d'information du Burkina TPT/ata

items.title: Aiyedatiwa to buy Dangote shares for 500 Ondo youths
items.description: By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has announced plans to acquire shares in the Dangote Group for 500 young entrepreneurs in the state as part of efforts to promote wealth creation and financial inclusion among youths. Aiyedatiwa disclosed this at the 2026 ONDEA Entrepreneurs Summit in Akure, where he said the beneficiaries would be selected from young entrepreneurs participating in the state’s enterprise development programmes. He said the initiative would give the beneficiaries an ownership stake in one of Africa’s major indigenous business groups while exposing them to capital market investment. The governor also launched the Lucky Light Initiative, which he said would provide solar power support to 1,000 small businesses across the state’s 18 local government areas. He clarified that the initiative was designed specifically as a business support intervention and not a household electrification programme. Aiyedatiwa further announced an N80 million grant for 20 entrepreneurs selected under the ONDEA My IDEA programme, with each beneficiary receiving N4 million. He said the beneficiaries would also receive mentorship, business support services and opportunities for foreign business exposure. According to the governor, the initiatives were part of his administration’s efforts to transform Ondo from a predominantly civil service economy into an entrepreneurship and innovation-driven state. “Our goal is to move beyond producing raw materials to processing, packaging, branding and exporting finished products for local and global markets,” he said. The summit was themed, “Positioning Entrepreneurs for Emerging Opportunities.” In his keynote address, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, represented by his Special Adviser, Toba Oyedele, said entrepreneurs were critical to achieving Nigeria’s $1 trillion economy target by 2030. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Investment, Dr Summy Smart Francis, said the My IDEA initiative received more than 2,703 applications. He said 20 winners emerged after undergoing three stages of screening. Also speaking, media entrepreneur and former TVC Entertainment boss, Morayo Afolabi-Brown, urged investors to look beyond Lagos and explore business opportunities across the South-West. The post Aiyedatiwa to buy Dangote shares for 500 Ondo youths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mimiko urges Nigerians to demand accountability from governors
items.description: .. Floats coalition for Tinubu’s 2027 re-election By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Former Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) governorship candidate in Ondo State, Dr Abass Mimiko, has urged Nigerians to demand accountability from state governors over increased allocations accruing to states following the removal of petrol subsidy. Mimiko, younger brother of former Ondo State Governor Olusegun Mimiko, made the call while speaking with journalists in Ondo town at the weekend. He said the increased revenues available to states should translate into visible improvements in infrastructure and public services, including roads, healthcare, education and agriculture. Mimiko argued that citizens should not blame the Federal Government for every socio-economic challenge, but should also demand explanations from state governments on how public funds are being utilised. “It is not the President’s duty to come to a state and direct a governor to fix roads, fund primary healthcare or make education affordable,” he said. He added that Nigeria’s federal structure places substantial responsibilities and resources in the hands of sub-national governments, including local councils. “People must ask their governors: what are you doing with this huge allocation?” he said. Mimiko also urged governors and council chairmen to prioritise food production, arguing that increased agricultural output would help address hunger and other socio-economic pressures. He lamented the influence of vote-buying on elections, saying the practice could weaken citizens’ ability to demand accountability from elected leaders. Mimiko, however, called on President Bola Tinubu to ensure that funds released to states were properly utilised. On the 2027 presidential election, the former ZLP candidate announced plans to establish a support group for Tinubu’s re-election. He said the group, known as the One Love Coalition for Tinubu, would comprise ZLP members, student leaders and other supporters of the President who are not members of the All Progressives Congress (APC). “Tinubu does not belong to APC alone but to all Nigerians,” Mimiko said. He said the coalition would be inaugurated across the local government areas and senatorial districts in Ondo State, with a target of mobilising more than one million votes for Tinubu in 2027. Mimiko said he would serve as Director-General of the coalition and mobilise ethnic groups, religious leaders, students and market women for door-to-door campaigns. He said Tinubu deserved a second term, citing the continuation of the administration’s reforms and programmes, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), as reasons for his position. Mimiko also urged citizens to scrutinise how increased public revenues were being spent and to demand measurable results from elected officials at all levels of government. items.title: FRSC disowns viral recruitment notice
items.description: Warns applicants against fraudsters ABUJA — The Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC, has disowned a viral recruitment notice circulating on social media directing applicants who were not shortlisted or did not receive invitation messages to report to the nearest FRSC camp for verification. The Corps described the notice as fake and unauthorised, urging applicants to disregard it. In a statement, the FRSC said no directive had been issued asking applicants to report to any of its offices, camps or training institutions for verification on or before September 25, 2026. The Corps advised applicants participating in the 2026 recruitment exercise to rely only on its official communication channels for authentic information. It also warned applicants against making payments, sharing personal information or clicking links circulated by unauthorised persons claiming to facilitate their recruitment. The FRSC said anyone found using the recruitment exercise to deceive or defraud members of the public would be reported to the appropriate law-enforcement authorities. The Corps urged members of the public to disregard the fraudulent publication and exercise caution to avoid falling victim to recruitment scams. items.title: Africa World Airlines unveils first Embraer E190 as part of 10-aircraft fleet expansion
items.description: Africa World Airlines (AWA) has unveiled its first Embraer E190 aircraft as part of a planned 10-aircraft fleet expansion aimed at strengthening air connectivity in Ghana and across West Africa. The 102-seat aircraft, unveiled at the Accra International Airport under the theme “Expanding Horizons, Elevating West African Connectivity”, has 14 premium economy and 88 economy seats. Chief Executive of AWA, Luolin Cui, said the aircraft marked a new chapter for the airline and would support its ambition to expand its regional operations. “Every aircraft should tell a Ghanaian story. Every aircraft should carry a Ghanaian pride,” he said. Mr Cui said the E190 was the first of 10 aircraft planned for the fleet expansion, which is expected to improve connectivity across the sub-region. He said 97% of AWA’s workforce was Ghanaian and that the airline had carried more than five million passengers since beginning operations in 2012. Domestic aviation faces high operating costs Speaking on behalf of AWA Executive Chairman, Tobe Afede XIV, Managing Director of the World Trade Centre Accra, Yvonne Botchey said the investment came amid significant challenges in Ghana’s domestic aviation sector. She said the cost of operating local airlines was affected by the heavy reliance on imported inputs, foreign exchange costs and customs duties. Ms Botchey also cited limited passenger numbers and airport operating hours as factors affecting aircraft utilisation and the profitability of domestic airlines. According to her, AWA paid its first dividend after 13 years of operations, highlighting the difficulty of operating an airline in the country. “AWA has come to stay,” she said. Government outlines aviation infrastructure plans Representing President John Dramani Mahama, Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe said the government was investing in aviation infrastructure to expand capacity and improve connectivity. He said a connecting concourse between Terminals 2 and 3 at Kotoka International Airport was expected to make transfers between domestic, regional and international flights easier. He also said airport infrastructure was being developed in Bolgatanga, Wa and Sunyani, while the runway at Kumasi International Airport was being expanded to accommodate larger aircraft. Mr Nikpe said the government was gradually extending operating hours at some airports as part of efforts to support the 24-hour economy. He also urged domestic airlines to reflect recent government measures, including the waiver of duties on aircraft spare parts, in fares. “We want to seize this opportunity to appeal to all the airlines, to also look at the fares and let it reflect on the Ghanaian traveller,” he said. Tourism Minister highlights regional connectivity Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts Minister Abla Dzifa Gomashie said improved air connectivity was critical to the growth of tourism and cultural exchange. She said AWA’s fleet expansion could make it easier for tourists and other travellers to move within Ghana and across the West African region. “Connectivity is the lifeblood of tourism and cultural exchange,” she said. Ms Gomashie noted that travel between African countries could still require lengthy and inefficient routes, and said improved intra-African connectivity would support tourism and economic activity. She commended AWA’s investment in the E190, saying it aligned with Ghana’s ambition to strengthen its position as a regional hub for air travel and tourism. The new aircraft comes as AWA marks 14 years of operations and follows the relaunch of its Accra-Abidjan route in July.
